newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Guangdong Power plans new B share issue.
newsitem.headline: Guangdong Power plans new B share issue.

text.p: Guangdong Electric Power Development Co Ltd has a preliminary plan to offer additional B shares to finance expansion of its 51 percent-owned Zhanjiang Power Plant, a company spokesman said on Friday.
"Guangdong Power is contacting the relevant authorities on the new B share issue," the spokesman told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
Proceeds from the offer will be used to double the number of Zhanjiang Plant's generators to four, each with 300,000 kw capacity, he said.
The expansion plan, which needs total investment of 3.2 billion yuan, is being reviewed by the State Planning Commission, the official said.
"We hope the third generator can become operational by 1999 and the fourth the year after," he said.
Guangdong Power expects electricity output of 6.71 billion kw hours for 1997, up from 5.81 billion in 1996, the official said.
"Output is expected to be boosted by the company's Meixian B Power Plant, which started operation last month with one 125,000-kw generator," the official said.

"A second generator in the plant with the same capacity will become operational by the end of this year," he added. "Our 1997 net profit will rise in line with the anticipated increase in electricity output, barring any major change in electricity rates," the official said but did not elaborate.
The company on Friday posted net profits of 563.75 million yuan for 1996, compared with 376.97 million based on international accounting standards.
The firm attributed the earnings surge to a 30 percent jump in electricity output.

The company proposed to make a two-for-10 bonus share issue and a cash dividend of 0.2 yuan per share based on 1996 profits, pending approval of shareholders scheduled to meet on May 16, the company's 1996 annual report said.
Guangdong Power is enjoying a two-year tax break begun in 1996 after it obtained the status of a foreign-invested company due to its issue of foreign currency B shares.
"We will apply for a 7.5 percent corporate tax rate after 1998," the official said. Most of China's listed companies are assessed at 15 percent.

The company had 825.45 million shares outstanding at end-1996, consisting of 513.65 million non-listed shares, 98.55 million domestic currency A shares and 213.25 million B shares, according to the firm's 1996 report.
